title: Embeddings and vector stores
summary: This intermediate module teaches you to design an embedding-based retrieval workflow, choose between exact and approximate search, and evaluate whether retrieved records are useful. After completing it, you can describe and troubleshoot the path from source content to vectors, stored records, similarity search, and retrieved context.
objectives: Explain how an embedding represents an input as a numeric vector for similarity comparison.
Design a vector-store record that connects an embedding to its source content and provenance.
Trace a query through embedding, similarity search, filtering, and content retrieval.
Choose between exact and approximate nearest-neighbor search for a stated retrieval requirement.
Evaluate retrieval with labeled queries and diagnose failures involving segmentation, representation, search, or source content.

It introduces the vector-search concepts it uses and does not assume prior knowledge of machine-learning training or advanced linear algebra. sections.title: What an embedding represents
paragraphs: An embedding procedure maps an input, such as text, to a fixed-length numeric vector. Research on distributed representations demonstrates that learned vectors can encode relationships that support similarity comparisons. Sources: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality, https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.4546, checked 2026-08-20; Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs, https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08734, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

The vector is useful because a retrieval system can compare it with other vectors. Individual coordinates should not be treated as independently authored labels. The useful information is distributed across the representation and interpreted through comparisons in its vector space. Source: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality, https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.4546, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

A query vector and stored vectors must be created by compatible embedding procedures that place them in a shared comparison space. Retrieval-augmented generation research demonstrates this pattern with a query encoder and a dense vector index of documents. Source: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Treat the embedding procedure and the source record as separate parts of the design. The procedure creates a representation for comparison, while the source record supplies the content, identifier, and provenance that an application needs after retrieval. sections.callout: An embedding is a representation used for comparison. It is not the original content, a citation, or proof that the content is correct.

sections.title: What the vector store must retain
paragraphs: In this module, a vector store means a data system that retains vectors and enough associated information to find the corresponding source records. A practical record design contains a stable record identifier, the vector, the retrievable content or a resolvable content locator, and provenance such as a source identifier. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

The vector supports candidate selection, but the identifier or locator reconnects a candidate to usable content. Dense retrieval research follows this separation by searching a vector index and then using the retrieved documents as non-parametric memory. Source: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. Metadata can be retained for application rules such as access scope, document type, language, or publication state. Decide which fields are required before indexing, because a vector alone does not contain the source record or its operational provenance. When source content changes, use a defined update process for both the source record and its vector. This is a design rule: the stored representation and the content returned for that record should refer to the same indexed state. sections.title: Preparing content for indexing
paragraphs: Long source material is commonly divided into retrieval units before embedding. Retrieval-augmented generation research demonstrates retrieval over document passages held in a dense vector index. Segmentation defines what one search result can return. A very broad unit may mix several subjects, while a narrow unit may omit context needed to interpret the passage. These are possible failure modes to test rather than universal size rules. For each unit, preserve a stable link to its parent source and enough location information to recover context. Then create its embedding and store the vector with the record identifier and provenance. Do not claim one universally correct unit size. sections.title: Similarity and nearest-neighbor search
paragraphs: Similarity search receives a query vector and looks for stored vectors that are closest according to a chosen comparison rule. Published similarity-search research describes nearest-neighbor retrieval over large vector collections and evaluates both Euclidean-distance and inner-product search settings. Source: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs, https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.08734, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

The comparison rule is part of the retrieval design because it determines what closest means. Use the rule intended for the embedding procedure, and keep that rule consistent while comparing evaluation results. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Exact search examines the collection sufficiently to identify the true nearest results under the selected rule. Approximate nearest-neighbor methods trade a guarantee of exact results for more efficient search over large collections. Research on hierarchical navigable small-world graphs evaluates this trade-off using search performance and recall. Source: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs, https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320, checked 2026-08-20.

Choose exact search when exact nearest results are required and the workload permits it. Consider approximate search when measured retrieval quality remains acceptable and search efficiency is a binding requirement. This decision must be based on measurements from the intended collection and queries rather than on an assumed universal threshold. sections.title: Tracing a retrieval request
paragraphs: A retrieval request can be traced through five conceptual stages. First, validate the query and any application constraints. Second, create a query embedding with a procedure compatible with the indexed vectors. Third, search for nearby vectors under the selected comparison rule. Fourth, apply required record-selection rules at a defined point in the workflow. Fifth, resolve the selected identifiers to source content and return the content with provenance.

Dense retrieval research supports the central sequence of encoding a query, searching a dense vector index, and retrieving documents for downstream use. Source: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401, checked 2026-08-20. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. When system constraints or rate limits are approached, explicit retry strategies with exponential backoff and jitter prevent cascading failures across downstream dependencies.

Record-selection rules and vector similarity answer different questions. Similarity ranks candidates under the vector comparison, while a selection rule decides whether a record is eligible for the request. Document whether eligibility is enforced before or after candidate generation so that missing results can be diagnosed. sections.title: Evaluating retrieval quality
paragraphs: Build a test set of representative queries with judgments identifying acceptable source records. For a selected result count, mark a query successful when at least one acceptable record appears in the returned set. Report the number of successful queries divided by the number of evaluated queries, and retain the individual failures for inspection. In production environments, engineers must account for token utilization patterns, context window pressure, and deterministic execution boundaries. Approximate nearest-neighbor research uses recall to measure how well approximate results reproduce desired neighbors, demonstrating that retrieval quality and search performance should be measured together. Source: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs, https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.09320, checked 2026-08-20. Diagnose a failed query in stages. Check whether the needed content exists in the indexed sources, whether segmentation produced a useful retrieval unit, whether the compatible embedding procedure was used, whether record-selection rules excluded the target, whether approximate search missed a desired neighbor, and whether the chosen result count was sufficient. A nearby vector is not automatically a correct answer. It is a candidate selected under the embedding representation and comparison rule. Downstream use should preserve source provenance and apply any separate checks required by the application. questions.prompt: Which record design best supports returning usable source content after a similarity search?
choices: Store only the vector because its coordinates contain the complete source record.
Store the vector with a stable record identifier and source content or a resolvable content locator.
Store only the query that was used to create the vector.
Store a similarity score permanently without retaining source provenance.
questions.explanation: The module specifies that the vector selects candidates, while an identifier, content field, or resolvable locator reconnects each candidate to usable source content and provenance.

questions.prompt: Why must query vectors and stored vectors be created by compatible embedding procedures?
choices: So they occupy a shared comparison space in which similarity search is meaningful.
So every source record has identical text.
So record identifiers can be removed.
So approximate search always returns exact results.
questions.explanation: The module states that query and stored vectors need compatible embedding procedures that place them in a shared comparison space.

questions.prompt: When is approximate nearest-neighbor search an appropriate choice according to this module?
choices: Whenever no retrieval evaluation is available.
When exact results are mandatory regardless of workload.
When measured retrieval quality is acceptable and search efficiency is a binding requirement.
When the source content has no stable identifiers.
questions.explanation: The module recommends considering approximate search only when its measured retrieval quality remains acceptable and efficiency is a binding requirement.

questions.prompt: A relevant source exists, but no acceptable record is retrieved. Which diagnostic sequence best follows the module?
choices: Inspect segmentation, embedding compatibility, selection rules, approximate-search behavior, and the selected result count.
Assume that a nearby vector must contain the correct answer.
Remove provenance fields and repeat the same request.
Judge retrieval only by the fluency of a downstream generated answer.
questions.explanation: The module directs the learner to inspect the retrieval pipeline in stages, including segmentation, representation, eligibility rules, search behavior, and result count.
